title: Daily Activities and Independence in Parkinson's
content: Parkinson's disease can gradually affect everyday activities such as dressing, bathing, eating, walking, writing, household tasks and other activities that require movement, coordination or balance. The level of difficulty varies between individuals and can change over time. Strategies that simplify tasks, allow more time, improve organization and support safe movement can help people remain as independent as possible. Occupational therapists and physical therapists can assess specific difficulties and suggest practical adaptations. A sudden or major decline in the ability to perform daily activities should be medically evaluated.
